player.name: Corvin Vale
player.concept: a silver-tongued human bard who treats every conversation as a negotiation
player.build: human bard 3 (College of Lore), criminal background

established: Sewn into the lining of Prout's left boot was a page razored from the Royal Granary Roll: a dozen grain wagons for the King's Road this past month marked 'lost to goblins', each countersigned 'J. Sallow, for the Royal Purveyor', with Prout's pencilled note beside each of what the same wagon weighed at the river warehouses two days later, and at the foot: 'Not goblins. Who pays the hedge-folk?'
Cob lets Corvin inspect his left boot; the boot remains Cob's.
The folded page from the boot is found and read.
Cob gives Corvin the page in exchange for one silver

opened.title: J. Sallow and the Purveyor's office

rulings.act: Press Cob to remove the boot; appeal to Moll for leverage
rulings.changed: Cob scowls, then sits on the water butt and unlaces his left boot, holding it out for you to inspect. The lining holds a folded, stiff page sewn in with small neat stitches; Cob takes the boot straight back; the scene went to What Prout found; came out: page

rulings.act: Ask Kell who Sallow is and where the Purveyor’s office is; offer Cob a silver for the page
rulings.changed: Cob pockets the silver and hands you the folded page, keeping the boot. Kell answers your questions: she knows J. Sallow’s name from Purveyor’s office notices, but doesn’t know which man he is or where his office is

rulings.act: Ask Moll who was in the yard last night
rulings.why: not like this: it's too far from what would move them (dangerous, weak, hostile)
rulings.changed: The girl in the shawl said no, and nothing else changed
